title: Training Note: Response Window, Intent Options and As-Is Appraisal Settings in Maturity and Due-and-Payable Cases
content:
This training note gives the Maturity and Due-and-Payable Cases plan settings for the borrower's or successor's response, the resolution intents that may be declared, and the as-is appraisal.

| Case plan | Response window after the due-and-payable notice | As-is appraisal ordered within (after the loan is called due) | Months an as-is appraisal stays usable |
|---|---|---|---|
| Death of Last Surviving Borrower | 30 calendar days | 30 calendar days | 6 months |
| Sale or Title Transfer | 30 calendar days | 30 calendar days | 6 months |
| Extended Health-Care Absence | 30 calendar days | 30 calendar days | 6 months |
| Principal Residence Change | 30 calendar days | 30 calendar days | 6 months |
| Property Charge Default | 30 calendar days | 30 calendar days | 6 months |
| Property Condition Default | 30 calendar days | 30 calendar days | 6 months |

Under every plan, the resolution intents a borrower or successor may declare are:

- keep the property (retention, by paying the loan off);
- sell the property;
- a deed in lieu of foreclosure.

Under every plan, when no intent is declared within the response window, the case proceeds toward its resolution deadline.

## Questions trainees ask

**How many intents may be declared?** One of the three listed. No plan offers any other option.

**What does "usable for six months" mean?** Under every plan, an as-is appraisal remains usable for resolution for 6 months; after that a new one is ordered.

**Does any plan give a longer response window?** No. All six plans set the response window at 30 calendar days.

**Hypothetical illustration.** Suppose a loan is called due on an invented date, 3 March of some year. Under any plan, the as-is appraisal is ordered no later than 30 calendar days after that day, by 2 April. The response window is likewise 30 calendar days.
